name: NY-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 district lean strongly favors Democrats
Incumbent Latimer holds a large cash edge; Cinquemani has reported no fundraising
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 96%
No public polls or expert ratings, keeping the margin estimate wide
model.rationale: A district leaning 18 points Democratic, an incumbent Democrat with roughly $100,000 on hand, and a Republican challenger who has reported no money leave little plausible path to an upset, and markets price the Democratic win near 96%. With no polling available, the margin estimate stays wide, but the seat remains safely Democratic.
model.watch: A late influx of Republican outside spending or an unexpected controversy involving Latimer would be the main thing that could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New York's 16th District leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan lean of about 18 points, and incumbent Democrat George Latimer is seeking re-election against Republican Joseph Cinquemani, who has reported no fundraising. Latimer has raised about $514,000 and holds roughly $100,000 on hand. No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and market pricing.

Prediction markets put Latimer's chances around 96%, and the combination of a strong Democratic lean, incumbency, and a large financial edge makes an upset unlikely. The real uncertainty is the size of the margin rather than the winner, since sparse polling keeps the estimate broad. The seat rates as Safe Democratic.
